co_residency: three llama/whisper servers resident and idle; operator declared the system idle and authorized the window
notes: SOLID: unidirectional H2D 28.89 GB/s and D2H 28.20 GB/s, agreeing across all four NUMA nodes to within 0.1%, with a clean saturation curve (25.40 at 1 MB rising to 28.89 at 128 MB). Bulk host<->device transfer is NUMA-node-INDEPENDENT on this system.

SOLID: this settles the link generation. 28.89/31.5 = 91.7% of PCIe Gen4 x16 theoretical. The ~64 GB/s (Gen5) figure circulating in our docs is wrong by 2.2x; the ~26 GB/s figure was approximately right.

NOT A FINDING, an open question: bidirectional aggregate shows NUMA node 0 consistently high (50.89, 48.05) while the others are NOISY across passes - node 1 (33.89, 34.54), node 2 (33.15, 33.41), node 3 (40.44, 41.53, and 33.85/36.40/48.31 in an earlier unmatched pass). With n=2-3 per node and no CI this does not support a per-node ranking. Only the node-0 outlier is reproducible.

The node-0 outlier is NOT explained by device locality: the MI210 is on NUMA node 1, verified three ways (/sys/class/drm/card2/device 0x740f, /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:43:00.0/numa_node = 1, KFD topology node 4). Hypotheses NOT tested: independent placement of the two concurrent copy threads by the runtime; differing free-memory/fragmentation state per node (node 0 had 2266 MB free vs node 1's 22839 MB at measurement time); IOMMU path differences.
Buffers capped at 128 MB because only ~0.4 GiB VRAM was free with three servers resident. H2D/D2H saturate far below that, so the plateau is real and the cap does not bound the result.
Agent-index-to-NUMA-node mapping VERIFIED 1:1 via rocminfo (Agent 1 = Node 0 ... Agent 4 = Node 3, GPU = Node 4) rather than assumed.
open_questions: Why is bidirectional aggregate from NUMA node 0 ~48% higher than from the device-local node 1? Needs repeated passes with a stated n and CI before it is treated as a placement input.
relevance_to_G1: The GPU lane's host threads are pinned at CPUs 184-191, which numactl places on NUMA node 3 - neither the device-local node (1) nor the bidirectional-fastest node (0). Unidirectional transfer being node-independent means that placement costs nothing on the BULK TRANSFER path; it says nothing about host-side memory access during serving, which is the regime G1 actually targets.
